paraphrase: Bounded conditional laws and countermodels for issue #248: H and C(¬H) yield ◇¬H and conflict with □H, but are jointly satisfiable without □H. Full-function local collapse separates accessible worlds; on symmetric transitive components possible collapse implies collapse and excludes independently instantiated contingency, so H with C(MC) excludes such contingency. The bridge can fail, weaker reflexive transitive frames invalidate propagation, narrow withholding can coexist with a bridge, and collapse need not mean globally unique worlds. Exact quantifiers and model witnesses are in Checks; no result refutes Hume or asserts real-world contingency.
